source.authors: Damiano F. G. Fiorillo, Alessandro Lella, Ciaran A. J. O’Hare, Edoardo Vitagliano
source.title: Leading Bounds on Micrometer to Picometer Fifth Forces from Neutron Star Cooling

results.scalar_nucleon_coupling: g_N <= 5e-14 in the strongest part of the mass range; explicitly quoted for m_phi <= 100 eV
results.confidence: 95% CL; Fig. 1 is a mass-dependent limit curve

source.mechanism: Scalar emission by nucleons in old isolated neutron stars accelerates cooling; observed luminosities and ages are compared with modeled cooling curves.

mapping_to_tpl.warning: The P3 coefficient implied by f_N=0.30 is about 1.43 times the source paper's quoted Higgs-portal coefficient. Reconcile the hadronic form-factor convention and uncertainty before precision combination; do not silently equate the normalizations.
mapping_to_tpl.logic: Use the source's headline mixing-angle translation as an approximate screen. The exact 95% CL g_N limit is mass-dependent in Fig. 1; this record does not digitize or interpolate the curve.

points.interpretation: 10 eV lies below 100 eV; the article explicitly states g_N <= 5e-14 in this low-mass region.

10 keV lies in the eV-to-MeV mass domain and below 700 keV, where the article says neutron-star cooling bounds dominate prior astrophysical limits. The precise limit at this mass is on Fig. 1 and is not digitized here.
10 MeV exceeds the paper's approximate eV-to-MeV domain; no inference from this source.

parameter_logic: The input sin(theta) <= 1e-6 is only an upper cap, not a measured value. At the reference test point sin(theta)=1e-6, 10 eV and 10 keV exceed the published Higgs-portal summary bound. The paper's summary tightens the allowed upper range to about 6e-11 in the covered light-mass region; smaller actual mixing values are not automatically excluded. 10 MeV is outside this source's range.
caveats: Neutron-star cooling constraints depend on neutron-star equation of state, superfluidity, envelope composition, nuclear interaction model and heating assumptions.
The authors estimate a factor 2-3 uncertainty on final coupling constraints from nuclear emissivity uncertainties.
The source Higgs-portal normalization differs from P3's f_N=0.30 default and requires reconciliation before a precision combined fit.
No global combination with laboratory neutron scattering or other astrophysical probes was performed.
The precise 10 keV limit was not digitized from Fig. 1; the helper applies the headline mixing-angle translation as a screening bound.
